# Simulation study of bootstrap procedures

## Data-generating process and experimental factors

The simulation uses 226 equally spaced annual observations and a central
true break at index 113:

$$y_t=9.5-0.05x_t+\delta(x_t-x_{113})_++\varepsilon_t,\quad
x_t=(t-\bar t)/10,$$

$$\varepsilon_t=\rho\varepsilon_{t-1}+\sigma_tu_t,\qquad u_t\sim N(0,1).$$

Eight scenarios cross $\delta\in\{0,0.14\}$, $\rho\in\{0,0.4\}$ and
constant or increasing innovation scale. When $\delta=0$, rejection
frequency estimates **size** under the no-break null; when
$\delta=0.14$, it estimates **power**. The slope change approximates the
empirical estimate.

The common innovation scale is calibrated from the empirical
broken-model residual standard deviation,
$\widehat\sigma=\sqrt{RSS_1/(n-3)}$. For the increasing profile, scales
ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 are normalized to have mean square one. This
matches average innovation variance across scale conditions; it does not
fix marginal error variance across values of $\rho$.

Initialization is stationary for constant scale and a local
initialization for changing scale. Unlike the empirical design, the
simulated calendar has no missing years; it isolates the selected
dependence and variance factors.

```{r simulation-data-generator}
simulate_broken_trend <- function(design, delta, rho, heteroskedastic,
                                  sigma, alpha = 9.5, beta = -0.05,
                                  break_index = floor(design$n / 2)) {
  n <- design$n
  scale_profile <- if (heteroskedastic) seq(0.5, 1.5, length.out = n) else rep(1, n)
  # Match average innovation variance across variance-profile conditions.
  scale_profile <- scale_profile / sqrt(mean(scale_profile^2))
  sigma_t <- sigma * scale_profile
  u <- rnorm(n)
  error <- numeric(n)
  # Stationary initialization under the initial innovation scale. For changing
  # sigma_t this is a local initialization, not global stationarity.
  error[1L] <- sigma_t[1L] * u[1L] / sqrt(1 - rho^2)
  for (i in 2L:n) error[i] <- rho * error[i - 1L] + sigma_t[i] * u[i]
  alpha + beta * design$x +
    delta * pmax(0, design$x - design$x[break_index]) + error
}
```

## Monte Carlo uncertainty

If $r$ of $M$ datasets reject, the rejection frequency is
$\widehat p=r/M$ and its Monte Carlo standard error is
$\sqrt{\widehat p(1-\widehat p)/M}$. We also report Wilson intervals.
Unlike a plug-in standard error, these remain informative at a rejection
rate of 100%. They measure uncertainty in simulation frequencies, not
empirical slope uncertainty.

```{r wilson-interval}
wilson_interval <- function(successes, trials, level = 0.95) {
  z <- qnorm((1 + level) / 2)
  p <- successes / trials
  den <- 1 + z^2 / trials
  ctr <- (p + z^2 / (2 * trials)) / den
  half <- z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / trials + z^2 / (4 * trials^2)) / den
  c(lower = max(0, ctr - half), upper = min(1, ctr + half))
}
```

## Run and checkpoint all scenarios

Every scenario uses $M=1,000$ datasets, and each dataset receives all
three bootstrap tests with $B=499$. This totals 8,000 datasets, 24,000
tests and 11,976,000 bootstrap draws. DWB uses bandwidth six.

Dataset $m$ in scenario $c$ receives seed $20260926+100000c+m$.
Consequently, changing worker scheduling does not change its random
stream. Methods use the same simulated datasets. Each complete scenario
is checkpointed together with every setting affecting its statistical
computation. Checkpoints with changed settings are recomputed, and an
incomplete scenario is not accepted.

```{r simulation-engine}
run_simulation <- function(M = 1000L, B = 499L, n = 226L,
                           sigma = NULL, seed = 20260926L,
                           workers = min(4L, parallel::detectCores()),
                           checkpoint_dir = "work/simulation",
                           summary_file = "tables/simulation_summary.csv",
                           raw_file = "work/simulation/simulation_results.rds",
                           resume = TRUE) {
  if (is.null(sigma)) {
    station <- read.csv(file.path(project_root, "Station08.csv"))
    station <- station[order(station$Year), ]
    empirical <- fit_break(station$Temperature, prepare_design(station$Year))
    sigma <- sqrt(empirical$RSS1 / (nrow(station) - 3L))
  }
  stopifnot(M >= 1000L, B >= 499L, n >= 10L, sigma > 0, workers >= 1L)
  design <- prepare_design(seq_len(n), trim = 0.15)
  settings <- list(M = as.integer(M), B = as.integer(B), n = as.integer(n),
                   sigma = sigma, seed = as.integer(seed), alpha = 9.5,
                   beta = -0.05, break_index = floor(n / 2),
                   trim = 0.15, level = 0.05, ell = round(n^(1/3)),
                   statistic = "raw RSS reduction", engine_version = 1L)
  scenarios <- expand.grid(delta = c(0, 0.14), rho = c(0, 0.4),
                           heteroskedastic = c(FALSE, TRUE),
                           KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)
  scenarios$config <- seq_len(nrow(scenarios))
  dir.create(checkpoint_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  dir.create(dirname(summary_file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  dir.create(dirname(raw_file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  all_raw <- vector("list", nrow(scenarios))
  start <- Sys.time()
  for (s in seq_len(nrow(scenarios))) {
    scenario <- scenarios[s, ]
    signature <- list(settings = settings, scenario = scenario)
    checkpoint <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, sprintf("config_%02d.rds", s))
    cached <- if (resume && file.exists(checkpoint)) readRDS(checkpoint) else NULL
    if (!is.null(cached) && identical(cached$signature, signature) &&
        nrow(cached$raw) == M) {
      all_raw[[s]] <- cached$raw
      message(sprintf("Scenario %d/8: reused verified complete checkpoint.", s))
      next
    }
    one_replication <- function(replication) {
      # Seeds do not depend on worker scheduling or the number of workers.
      replicate_seed <- as.integer(seed + s * 100000L + replication)
      set.seed(replicate_seed)
      y <- simulate_broken_trend(design, delta = scenario$delta,
                                 rho = scenario$rho,
                                 heteroskedastic = scenario$heteroskedastic,
                                 sigma = sigma)
      fit <- bootstrap_break(y, design, B = B, ell = settings$ell,
                             level = settings$level)
      out <- c(replication = replication, replicate_seed = replicate_seed,
               F = fit$observed$F, estimated_break_index = fit$observed$index)
      for (method in c("iid", "wild", "dwb")) {
        out[paste0(method, "_p")] <- fit$results[[method]]$p_value
        out[paste0(method, "_critical")] <- fit$results[[method]]$critical
        out[paste0(method, "_reject")] <- as.integer(fit$results[[method]]$reject)
      }
      out
    }
    replications <- if (.Platform$OS.type != "windows" && workers > 1L) {
      parallel::mclapply(seq_len(M), one_replication, mc.cores = workers,
                        mc.preschedule = TRUE, mc.set.seed = FALSE)
    } else lapply(seq_len(M), one_replication)
    if (any(vapply(replications, inherits, logical(1), "try-error")))
      stop("A simulation worker failed; no incomplete scenario was saved.")
    raw <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, replications))
    raw$config <- s
    raw$delta <- scenario$delta
    raw$rho <- scenario$rho
    raw$heteroskedastic <- scenario$heteroskedastic
    all_raw[[s]] <- raw
    saveRDS(list(signature = signature, raw = raw), checkpoint, version = 3)
    message(sprintf("Scenario %d/8 complete: delta=%.2f, rho=%.1f, heteroskedastic=%s; elapsed %.1f s.",
                    s, scenario$delta, scenario$rho, scenario$heteroskedastic,
                    as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start, units = "secs"))))
  }
  raw <- do.call(rbind, all_raw)
  rownames(raw) <- NULL
  summaries <- list()
  i <- 0L
  for (s in seq_len(nrow(scenarios))) for (method in c("iid", "wild", "dwb")) {
    i <- i + 1L
    subsample <- raw[raw$config == s, ]
    rejections <- sum(subsample[[paste0(method, "_reject")]])
    rate <- rejections / M
    interval <- wilson_interval(rejections, M)
    summaries[[i]] <- data.frame(config = s, delta = scenarios$delta[s],
      rho = scenarios$rho[s], heteroskedastic = scenarios$heteroskedastic[s],
      estimand = if (scenarios$delta[s] == 0) "size" else "power", method = method,
      M = M, B = B, n = n, sigma = sigma, seed = seed, ell = settings$ell,
      rejections = rejections, rejection_rate = rate,
      mc_se = sqrt(rate * (1 - rate) / M),
      lower_95 = unname(interval[1L]), upper_95 = unname(interval[2L]))
  }
  summary <- do.call(rbind, summaries)
  result <- list(settings = settings, scenarios = scenarios, raw = raw,
                 summary = summary, elapsed_seconds =
                   as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start, units = "secs")),
                 session_info = sessionInfo())
  write.csv(summary, summary_file, row.names = FALSE)
  saveRDS(result, raw_file, version = 3)
  message(sprintf("Saved %d replications, %d bootstrap tests, and %d summary rows.",
                  nrow(raw), nrow(raw) * 3L, nrow(summary)))
  invisible(result)
}
```

If `recompute_simulation` is `false`, completed scenario results from an
earlier run are reused only after the simulation engine has verified
that all their settings match the current design; otherwise every
scenario is computed afresh. Because each simulated dataset has its own
fixed seed, both routes give identical results.

```{r run-simulation, message=TRUE}
checkpoint_dir <- file.path("work", "simulation")
if (!params$recompute_simulation) {
  original_checkpoints <- list.files(
    file.path(project_root, "work", "simulation"),
    pattern = "^config_[0-9]{2}\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE
  )
  for (original in original_checkpoints) {
    target <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, basename(original))
    if (!file.exists(target)) {
      copied <- file.copy(original, target, overwrite = FALSE)
      if (!copied) stop("Could not copy a simulation checkpoint: ", original)
    }
  }
}
sigma <- sqrt(fast$RSS1 / (n - 3L))
simulation <- run_simulation(
  M = simulation_M, B = simulation_B, n = n,
  sigma = sigma, seed = master_seed, workers = workers,
  checkpoint_dir = checkpoint_dir,
  summary_file = "tables/simulation_summary.csv",
  raw_file = "work/simulation/simulation_results.rds",
  resume = !params$recompute_simulation
)
sim <- simulation$summary
knitr::kable(simulation$scenarios, caption = "Eight Monte Carlo configurations")
cat("Calibrated innovation scale:", sigma, "degrees C\n")
cat("Datasets:", nrow(simulation$raw),
    "; bootstrap tests:", 3L * nrow(simulation$raw),
    "; bootstrap samples:", 3L * nrow(simulation$raw) * simulation_B, "\n")
```

## Rejection frequencies and their interpretation

A well-calibrated nominal 5% test should reject approximately 5% of
no-break datasets. Power must be interpreted alongside size: a method
that rejects too often under the null can have misleadingly high
apparent power.

```{r simulation-results-table}
method_names <- c(iid = "IID residual", wild = "Independent wild", dwb = "Dependent wild")
simulation_comparison <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(sim$config), function(config) {
  z <- sim[sim$config == config, ]
  rates <- vapply(c("iid", "wild", "dwb"), function(method) {
    100 * z$rejection_rate[z$method == method]
  }, numeric(1L))
  data.frame(
    Configuration = config, Quantity = ifelse(z$delta[1] == 0, "Size", "Power"),
    Change = z$delta[1], Rho = z$rho[1],
    Innovation_scale = ifelse(z$heteroskedastic[1], "Increasing", "Constant"),
    IID_residual_percent = rates[1], Independent_wild_percent = rates[2],
    Dependent_wild_percent = rates[3], row.names = NULL
  )
}))
knitr::kable(simulation_comparison, digits = 1, caption = "Rejection frequencies (%)")
```

With independent, constant-variance errors, IID residual and independent
wild tests have sizes 4.1% and 4.3%. Under independence and increasing
variance, IID residual size rises to 8.8%, while independent wild
remains near nominal at 5.4%.

Serial correlation has a larger effect. At $\rho=0.4$, the independent
procedures reject 26.5–32.2% of no-break datasets across the scale
designs. Their resampling schemes remove the serial dependence affecting
the observed search statistic, making the simulated critical values too
small in these settings.

DWB null rejection rates are 2.1–3.5%. It avoids over-rejection here but
is conservative relative to 5%, rather than exactly calibrated. Its
power is 98.5–99.0% under independence and 74.6–78.5% with
autocorrelation. Higher apparent power from the independent methods
under serial correlation should not be read as superior performance
because their null sizes are distorted. Size-adjusted power is not
calculated.

```{r simulation-results-plot, fig.cap="Size and power; vertical lines are Wilson intervals for simulation frequencies."}
plot_pair("simulation_results", function() {
    par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5.2, 4.4, 2.4, 0.8), mgp = c(2.7, 0.7, 0), las = 1,
        col.axis = axis_colour, col.lab = label_colour,
        col.main = label_colour, cex = 0.8)
    cols <- c(gray, navy, teal)
    for (estimand in c("size", "power")) {
        z <- sim[sim$estimand == estimand, ]
        ks <- unique(z$config)
        ylim <- if (estimand == "size") 
            c(0, 40)
        else c(60, 103)
        plot(1, 1, type = "n", xlim = c(0.6, 4.4), ylim = ylim, xaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "Rejection frequency (%)", 
            main = ifelse(estimand == "size", "Null rejection (nominal 5%)", "Power (change 0.14 degrees C/decade)"))
        axis(1, at = 1:4, labels = c("Independent\nconstant", "AR(0.4)\nconstant", "Independent\nincreasing", 
            "AR(0.4)\nincreasing"), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.8)
        if (estimand == "size") 
            abline(h = 5, lty = 3, col = gray)
        for (j in 1:3) {
            zz <- z[z$method == c("iid", "wild", "dwb")[j], ]
            xx <- (1:4) + (j - 2) * 0.1
            lines(xx, 100 * zz$rejection_rate, type = "b", pch = 15 + j, col = cols[j], lwd = 1.4)
            segments(xx, 100 * zz$lower_95, xx, 100 * zz$upper_95, col = cols[j])
        }
        if (estimand == "size") 
            legend("topleft", c("IID residual", "Independent wild", "Dependent wild"), col = cols, 
                pch = 16:18, lty = 1, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
    }
}, 10, 4.6)

knitr::include_graphics(file.path(artifact_root, "figures/simulation_results.png"))

```

```{r simulation-uncertainty-table}
uncertainty_table <- data.frame(
  Configuration = sim$config, Quantity = sim$estimand,
  Procedure = unname(method_names[sim$method]), Rejections = sim$rejections,
  Frequency_percent = 100 * sim$rejection_rate,
  MC_SE_percentage_points = 100 * sim$mc_se,
  Wilson_lower_percent = 100 * sim$lower_95,
  Wilson_upper_percent = 100 * sim$upper_95
)
knitr::kable(uncertainty_table, digits = 2,
             caption = "Monte Carlo uncertainty for all 24 procedure–scenario combinations")
```

The simulation supports retaining dependence in station inference, but
it does not prove that the empirical DWB p-value is conservative. It
covers Gaussian innovations, one sample size, one reasonably strong
central kink and one DWB bandwidth. It does not evaluate missingness,
weak or multiple breaks, alternative dependence models or
confidence-interval coverage. Those limits temper direct transfer to the
irregular empirical record.

# Conclusion

The Geneva record from 1753 to 2013 shows a positive average linear
trend of `r fmt(beta1_hat, 4)` °C per decade, but a single straight line
is not an adequate description of it. The residuals of the linear model
are positively autocorrelated (Monte Carlo Durbin–Watson p =
`r fmt(p_val_dw)`), while there is no evidence of a trend in the
residual variance (Breusch–Pagan p = `r fmt(p_val_bp)`). Part of this
dependence reflects low-frequency movements that one slope cannot
capture.

A continuous broken trend fits best with a kink at `r year[k]` and
reduces the residual sum of squares by
`r fmt(100 * Fobs / sum(e0^2), 2)`%. It describes the record as a
slightly declining trend before the break (`r fmt(coef(m1)[2])` °C per
decade) followed by warming of `r fmt(sum(coef(m1)[2:3]))` °C per
decade. The selected year coincides with the coldest year in the record,
but excluding that year or the post-gap observations leaves the kink in
the mid-nineteenth century, a timing consistent with the end of the
Little Ice Age in the Alps.

The evidence that the trend actually changed is
`r if (btests$p_value[btests$method == "dwb" & !is.na(btests$ell) & btests$ell == 6] <= 0.05) "moderate" else "weak"`.
The primary dependent wild bootstrap
`r if (btests$p_value[btests$method == "dwb" & !is.na(btests$ell) & btests$ell == 6] <= 0.05) "rejects" else "does not reject"`
the no-break null at the 5% level (p =
`r fmt(btests$p_value[btests$method == "dwb" & !is.na(btests$ell) & btests$ell == 6])`),
but its p-value rises with the bandwidth to
`r fmt(btests$p_value[btests$method == "dwb" & !is.na(btests$ell) & btests$ell == 12])`
at $\ell=12$. Bootstrap procedures that ignore serial dependence reject
much more strongly, but their p-values are not credible given the
Section 3 diagnostics. Conditional on the broken-trend model,
`r if (all(cis$lower[cis$parameter == "pre"] <= 0 & cis$upper[cis$parameter == "pre"] >= 0)) "the pre-break slope is not distinguishable from zero" else "the pre-break slope differs from zero"`,
while
`r if (all(cis$lower[cis$parameter == "post"] > 0)) "the post-break slope is positive under both interval types" else "the post-break slope is not clearly positive"`.

The simulation study shows that independent-error bootstraps over-reject
substantially when errors are autocorrelated, whereas the DWB keeps size
at or below the nominal level at the cost of lower power. This supports
the choice of the DWB for this station, although it does not prove that
the empirical DWB p-value is conservative.

In answer to the research question, the Geneva record indicates warming
since the mid-nineteenth century of about
`r fmt(10 * sum(coef(m1)[2:3]), 2)` °C per century; a single linear
trend understates this warming by averaging it with an earlier cooler
phase; and there is moderate, bandwidth-sensitive statistical evidence
for a change in the trend. The main limitations are the missing years
1981–2009, station history beyond what homogenisation corrects, the
restriction to a single break and a single dependence model, and the
absence of a coverage study for the confidence intervals.

# Appendix A: Computational validation {.unnumbered}

The checks below are executable rather than asserted. They compare the
optimised break search with brute-force OLS, reconstruct both interval
types from the stored bootstrap draws, verify the finite-replication
p-value corrections, reconstruct every simulation rejection frequency
and Wilson interval, and replay one complete dataset from each of the
eight simulation scenarios. All functions used are defined in this
document, and the checks write only to its working folder.

## A.1 Section 3 computations {.unnumbered}

These checks verify that the 1850 centring and mean-year centring give
identical fitted lines and slopes, that the complete supplied sample is
retained, that an independent QR projection reproduces all 9,999 draws
for both DW definitions, and that the BP statistic agrees with its
one-regressor squared-correlation identity.

```{r part1-independent-checks}
original_data <- read.csv(file.path(project_root, "Station08.csv"))
stopifnot(identical(dat$Year, original_data$Year),
          identical(dat$Temperature, original_data$Temperature),
          n == 226L, length(missing_years) == 35L, nrow(gap_table) == 5L)
centered_model <- lm(Temperature ~ I((Year - mean(Year)) / 10), data = dat)
stopifnot(max(abs(fitted(centered_model) - fitted(trend_model))) < 1e-10,
          abs(coef(centered_model)[2] - beta1_hat) < 1e-12,
          abs(coef(centered_model)[1] + beta1_hat * (1850 - mean(dat$Year)) / 10 - beta0_hat) < 1e-12)

set.seed(master_seed)
Z_check <- matrix(rnorm(n * B), nrow = n)
Q_check <- qr.Q(qr(model.matrix(trend_model)))
E_check <- Z_check - Q_check %*% crossprod(Q_check, Z_check)
dw_replayed <- colSums((E_check[-1, , drop = FALSE] -
                        E_check[-n, , drop = FALSE])^2) / colSums(E_check^2)
dw_gap_replayed <- colSums((E_check[valid_pairs + 1L, , drop = FALSE] -
                            E_check[valid_pairs, , drop = FALSE])^2) / colSums(E_check^2)
stopifnot(max(abs(dw_replayed - d_sim)) < 1e-10,
          max(abs(dw_gap_replayed - d_sim_gap)) < 1e-10,
          abs(n * cor(dat$residual_sq, dat$t)^2 - BP_stat) < 1e-12)
part1_checks <- c(
  "PASS: all supplied rows, five gaps and 35 missing years are retained",
  "PASS: year-1850 and mean-year parameterizations have identical fitted lines and slopes",
  "PASS: independent QR projection reproduces both 9,999-draw DW reference distributions",
  "PASS: BP agrees with the one-regressor squared-correlation identity"
)
write_csv(dw_results, "tables/dw_comparison.csv")
writeLines(part1_checks, "outputs/part1_validation.txt")
cat(paste(part1_checks, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
```

## A.2 Break search, intervals and simulation {.unnumbered}

```{r independent-validation}
checks <- character()
pass <- function(text) {
  checks <<- c(checks, paste("PASS:", text))
  cat(tail(checks, 1L), "\n")
}
station <- read.csv(file.path(project_root, "Station08.csv"))
stopifnot(nrow(station) == 226L, !anyNA(station),
          !anyDuplicated(station$Year), all(diff(station$Year) > 0))
y <- station$Temperature
D <- prepare_design(station$Year)
fitted_break <- fit_break(y, D)
x <- D$x
rss_grid <- sapply(D$index, function(k)
  deviance(lm(y ~ x + I(pmax(0, x - x[k])))))
rss_null <- deviance(lm(y ~ x))
stopifnot(abs(fitted_break$F - (rss_null - min(rss_grid))) < 1e-9,
          fitted_break$index == D$index[which.min(rss_grid)],
          max(abs(fitted_break$fitted - fitted(lm(y ~ x +
            I(pmax(0, x - x[fitted_break$index])))))) < 1e-9)
pass("optimized break search agrees with independent brute-force OLS and fitted values")

set.seed(320926)
for (method in c("iid", "wild", "dwb")) {
  errors <- bootstrap_errors(fitted_break$null_residuals, D$year, 7L, method, 6, 2)
  projected <- break_statistics(errors, D)$F
  brute <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(errors)), function(b) {
    ystar <- fitted_break$null_fitted + errors[, b]
    rss0 <- deviance(lm(ystar ~ x))
    rss1 <- min(sapply(D$index, function(k)
      deviance(lm(ystar ~ x + I(pmax(0, x - x[k]))))))
    rss0 - rss1
  }, numeric(1L))
  stopifnot(max(abs(projected - brute)) < 1e-8)
}
pass("all 21 bootstrap checks reproduce full null-generated-series OLS statistics")

ci <- read.csv("tables/confidence_intervals.csv")
ci_draws <- read.csv("tables/ci_draws.csv")
stopifnot(nrow(ci_draws) == 4999L, nrow(ci) == 4L, !anyNA(ci_draws),
          all(ci$B == 4999L), all(ci$lower <= ci$upper),
          all(ci_draws$year %in% D$year[D$index]))
for (parameter in c("pre", "post")) {
  pc <- ci[ci$parameter == parameter & ci$type == "percentile", ]
  pt <- ci[ci$parameter == parameter & ci$type == "percentile_t", ]
  draws <- ci_draws[[parameter]]
  ses <- ci_draws[[paste0("se_", parameter)]]
  stopifnot(all(ses > 0), all(is.finite(ses)))
  percentile <- quantile(draws, c(.025, .975), type = 7, names = FALSE)
  tstar <- (draws - pt$estimate) / ses
  studentized <- pt$estimate - pt$hac_se *
    quantile(tstar, c(.975, .025), type = 7, names = FALSE)
  stopifnot(max(abs(percentile - c(pc$lower, pc$upper))) < 1e-10,
            max(abs(studentized - c(pt$lower, pt$upper))) < 1e-10)
}
pass("percentile and percentile-t intervals recompute from all 4,999 stored refits")

bt <- read.csv("tables/bootstrap_tests.csv")
stopifnot(nrow(bt) == 5L, all(bt$B == 9999L),
          all(abs(bt$statistic - fitted_break$F) < 1e-8),
          all(abs(bt$p_value - (1 + bt$exceedances) / (bt$B + 1)) < 1e-12))
pass("all reported empirical p-values follow the finite-replication correction")

simulation <- readRDS("work/simulation/simulation_results.rds")
raw <- simulation$raw
summary <- read.csv("tables/simulation_summary.csv")
stopifnot(nrow(raw) == 8000L, nrow(summary) == 24L, !anyNA(raw),
          all(table(raw$config) == 1000L), all(summary$M == 1000L),
          all(summary$B == 499L), all(summary$n == 226L),
          abs(simulation$settings$sigma - sqrt(fitted_break$RSS1 / 223)) < 1e-12)
for (s in seq_len(8L)) {
  one <- raw[raw$config == s, ]
  stopifnot(identical(sort(as.integer(one$replication)), seq_len(1000L)),
            all(one$replicate_seed == 20260926L + s * 100000L + one$replication))
  for (method in c("iid", "wild", "dwb")) {
    values <- one[[paste0(method, "_p")]]
    stopifnot(all(values >= 1 / 500 & values <= 1),
              all(abs(500 * values - round(500 * values)) < 1e-8))
    row <- summary[summary$config == s & summary$method == method, ]
    count <- sum(values <= .05)
    rate <- count / 1000
    interval <- wilson_interval(count, 1000)
    stopifnot(row$rejections == count, abs(row$rejection_rate - rate) < 1e-12,
      abs(row$mc_se - sqrt(rate * (1 - rate) / 1000)) < 1e-12,
      max(abs(c(row$lower_95, row$upper_95) - interval)) < 1e-12)
  }
}
pass("all 8,000 replications, 24 rejection rates, MC standard errors and Wilson intervals are consistent")

# Replay one observation from every scenario, independently of worker scheduling.
Ds <- prepare_design(seq_len(226L))
for (s in seq_len(8L)) {
  row <- raw[raw$config == s & raw$replication == 1000L, ]
  set.seed(row$replicate_seed)
  ys <- simulate_broken_trend(Ds, row$delta, row$rho, row$heteroskedastic,
                              simulation$settings$sigma)
  result <- bootstrap_break(ys, Ds, B = 499L)
  stopifnot(abs(result$observed$F - row$F) < 1e-10)
  for (method in c("iid", "wild", "dwb"))
    stopifnot(abs(result$results[[method]]$p_value - row[[paste0(method, "_p")]]) < 1e-12)
}
pass("recorded seeds reproduce one complete replication from every simulation scenario")
writeLines(checks, "outputs/validation.txt")
cat("All checks passed. Saved outputs/validation.txt.\n")
```

# Appendix B: Random seeds and session information {.unnumbered}

The Section 3 Monte Carlo test and its replay in Appendix A use seed
`r master_seed`. The empirical IID residual, independent wild and
primary DWB tests use the master seed `20260926` plus 101, 102 and 103.
The bandwidth checks use the master seed plus 203 and 212, and the slope
intervals use the master seed plus 301. Simulation dataset $m$ in
scenario $c$ uses `20260926 + 100000*c + m`, independently of worker
scheduling.

```{r session-record}
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = "outputs/sessionInfo.txt")
sessionInfo()
```

# Appendix C: Choice of reference year {.unnumbered}

The time index is $t=(\mathrm{Year}-1850)/10$; the division by ten
reports slopes per decade. The reference year 1850 was chosen because it
lies next to the estimated break date. The intercept of the linear model
is then the fitted temperature in 1850, and, since the estimated break
(`r year[k]`) does not precede 1850, the intercept of the broken-trend
model is also its fitted temperature in 1850. The two intercepts are
thus directly comparable at 1850. The fitted level at the estimated
turning point is instead $\widehat\alpha+\widehat\beta(\widehat T_1-1850)/10$.

Any other reference year, such as the sample mean, would change only the
intercept. Fitted values, residuals, slopes, the RSS, the break search
and all test statistics are invariant, as verified in Appendix A.1.
Centring at the sample mean would minimise the classical OLS variance of
the intercept, but no inference in this report concerns the intercept.
Because 1850 was chosen with knowledge of the Section 4 estimate, the
choice is purely presentational; although 1850 is also a common
pre-industrial reference year in climate assessments, it is not used
here in that sense.

# Appendix D: Effect of data gaps on the analysis {.unnumbered}

| Component | Effect of gaps | Approach retained or refined |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Exploratory and residual time plots | Observed lines must not imply data inside gaps | Lines are grouped by contiguous years; the largest gap is shaded |
| OLS estimates | Calendar spacing is represented, but coverage and missingness can matter | Retain $(\mathrm{Year}-1850)/10$ and the complete supplied sample |
| Residual ACF | Observation lags and calendar lags differ | Display both; calendar grid contains `NA` for absent years |
| Variance smooth | Its curve inside a gap is unsupported by observations there | Retain the descriptive smooth with an explicit limitation |
| QQ plot | Time order is absent from its construction | Treat it as a marginal descriptive comparison, not proof of Gaussianity |
| DW statistic and Monte Carlo | The specified formula uses observation adjacency | Primary specified statistic plus separately calibrated calendar-adjacent sensitivity |
| BP test | Algebra uses actual time; dependence qualifies its reference | Retain $nR^2$ and nominal $\chi^2_1$, with cautious non-rejection language |
| Section 4 bootstrap | Dependence should use actual calendar gaps | DWB multipliers depend on elapsed years; every sample repeats the date search |
| Overall interpretation | Missing decades and metadata limit conclusions | No inference about an unobserved trajectory, global change or physical cause |
